drivingQuestion: Does the prohibition of the sciatic nerve apply to the nerve in both thighs, or only to the nerve in one thigh (the right)?
outcomeNote: The Gemara settles the attribution: the anonymous mishna, which covers both thighs, is not Rabbi Yehuda's, whose baraita limits the prohibition to the right thigh; the baraita is left standing and unchallenged.

segments.he: בְּיָרֵךְ שֶׁל יָמִין וּבְיָרֵךְ שֶׁל שְׂמֹאל. מַתְנִיתִין לָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ נוֹהֵג אֶלָּא בְּאַחַת, וְהַדַּעַת מַכְרַעַת אֶת שֶׁל יָמִין.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches that the prohibition of the sciatic nerve applies «to» the «thigh of the right» leg «and to» the «thigh of the left» leg. The Gemara says: «The mishna is not in accordance with» the opinion of «Rabbi Yehuda, as it is taught» in a baraita that «Rabbi Yehuda says:» The prohibition of the sciatic nerve «applies only to» the sciatic nerve «in one» of the animal’s thighs, «and logic dictates» that it is «the right» thigh.
